findings.evidence: Line 81 `@[simp] theorem legendre_add_two`. Goal `(legendre (n+2)).natDegree = n+2` is closed by `natDegree_legendre` only if the argument is not expanded first; `(legendre (n+2)).eval 1 = 1` reduces under this simp set to `(n+2)⁻¹ * ((2n+3) - (n+1))`, which simp cannot finish. Mathlib's `Polynomial.Chebyshev.T_add_two` (mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Chebyshev.lean:107) is simp with a coefficient-free RHS that stays in the family, unlike the `C ((n+2:ℝ)⁻¹)` form here.
findings.fix: Remove `@[simp]` from `legendre_add_two`; keep it public as the `_def`-style recurrence to be used by explicit `rw`.
findings.issue: `@[simp] legendre_add_two` rewrites `legendre (n + 2)` to `C ((n+2)⁻¹) * (...)`, which is not a normal form; since simp rewrites subterms first, it blocks the file's own simp lemmas `natDegree_legendre` (194), `degree_legendre` (200), `leadingCoeff_legendre` (204), `coeff_legendre_self` (170), `legendre_eval_one` (120) and `legendre_ne_zero` (190) on any index of shape `n + 2`.

findings.evidence: The only in-repo use already works around it: Basic.lean:282-284 `... (1 - X ^ 2) (legendre m) (legendre n) (a := -1) (b := 1) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)`.
findings.fix: Make the endpoints explicit: `(w p q : ℝ[X]) (a b : ℝ) (ha : w.eval a = 0) (hb : w.eval b = 0)`.
findings.issue: `integral_derivative_mul_derivative_mul_eq_integral_mul_derivative_mul_derivative` takes the endpoints `{a b : ℝ}` implicit, inferable only from the vanishing hypotheses; when those are discharged by a tactic the endpoints are unsolved metavariables, so every consumer must pass them by name.

summary: The surface is otherwise minimal, complete and free of compatibility artifacts, but `@[simp]` on the solved recurrence `legendre_add_two` expands `legendre (n+2)` before the file's other simp lemmas can fire, shadowing `natDegree_legendre`, `degree_legendre`, `leadingCoeff_legendre`, `coeff_legendre_self`, `legendre_eval_one` and `legendre_ne_zero`. The general Sturm-Liouville lemma also forces named arguments at every call site.
